questions.explain: The chapter lists four layers: Signal Aggregation, Policy Evaluation, Action Executor, and Feedback and Circuit Breaking — the feedback layer verifies the intended effect and escalates to a human when exhausted.
options: Signal Aggregation, Policy Evaluation, Action Executor
Observation, Inference, Alerting, Escalation
Signal Aggregation, Policy Evaluation, Action Executor, Circuit Breaking
Signal Aggregation, Policy Evaluation, Action Executor, Feedback and Circuit Breaking
questions.q: What are the four layers of the reference autonomous database control plane?

questions.explain: The chapter states the cooldown mechanism is the circuit breaker that prevents action storms where a runaway policy fires continuously on a table not responding to corrective action.
options: To reduce the polling interval of signal collection to under 15 seconds
To prevent action storms where a runaway policy fires continuously on a table that is not responding to corrective action
To throttle the number of alerts sent to the on-call engineer
To batch multiple index rebuilds into a single transaction
questions.q: In the Python control-plane example, what is the purpose of the policy cooldown_seconds mechanism?

questions.explain: For fragmentation >= 40% the code uses REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON, SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON); below that it uses REORGANIZE.
options: REBUILD for moderate fragmentation and REORGANIZE for severe
Both REORGANIZE and REBUILD together
REORGANIZE for moderate fragmentation and REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON, SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON) for severe (>=40%)
Always REBUILD with MAXDOP = 1
questions.q: In the chapter's autonomous index remediation example, which operation is chosen when fragmentation is severe (>= 40%)?

questions.explain: The governance gate specifies autonomous execution for adding a non-clustered index off-peak below 50M rows off replication; dropping an unused index needs async approval; DDL on FK-related tables needs synchronous approval.
options: Adding a non-clustered index during off-peak hours when estimated row count is below 50 million and the table is not part of an active replication subscription
Dropping an unused index identified by a 30-day zero-usage window
Any DDL change affecting a table with a foreign key relationship to a table owned by a different team
Promoting a synchronous-commit secondary
questions.q: Which action does the chapter's governance gate allow for fully autonomous execution?

questions.explain: The chapter states LLMs belong at the recommendation generation stage, not execution; the LLM advisory sits between policy evaluation and human notification, annotating escalations, never initiating or approving actions.
options: Executing ALTER TABLE statements directly on production
Replacing the deterministic policy engine in the hot decision path
Annotating escalations with synthesized context for the on-call engineer (advisory layer only)
Approving supervised Tier 2 actions instead of a human veto
questions.q: Where does the chapter place LLMs in the autonomous control plane, and why?

title: The Evolution from AI-Driven DBA to Autonomous DBA
